programme: HOXC8 partners with SMAD1 at BMP-responsive elements — HOXC8's own target list (SMAD1, SMAD6, BMP2, SPP1/osteopontin, TNFRSF11B) is essentially the canonical BMP-SMAD1 target set — forming a homeodomain/SMAD complex that gates whether BMP signaling drives or restrains differentiation of a tissue's progenitor/repair pool.
role_in_a: In multiple sclerosis, SMAD1-transduced BMP signaling (BMP7 loss triggers oligodendrocyte apoptosis and demyelination; BMP-SMAD crosstalk disrupts the blood-CNS barrier) restrains oligodendrocyte precursor differentiation, so chronic or dysregulated activity of this axis leaves demyelinated lesions unable to remyelinate; its shared target osteopontin (SPP1) is a known driver of the MS lesion's neuroinflammatory environment.
role_in_b: In Sjögren's syndrome, the same SMAD1-driven BMP programme is engaged during repair of exocrine gland tissue after inflammatory injury (documented in lacrimal gland); persistent autoimmune attack that keeps this axis chronically deregulated would leave glandular acinar/ductal epithelium unable to regenerate, contributing to the progressive secretory failure (dry eye, dry mouth) that defines the disease.
shared_axis: MS and Sjögren's both involve repeated immune-mediated injury to a tissue that depends on a local progenitor pool for repair — oligodendrocytes in CNS white matter, acinar/ductal cells in exocrine glands — and the HOXC8-SMAD1 BMP programme is the signal that decides whether that pool differentiates and repairs the damage or stalls. The two diseases would converge on this axis not through a shared immune trigger but because both depend on BMP-restrained tissue renewal to cap damage from otherwise structurally similar autoimmune insults.
reasoning: MS's dependence on BMP-SMAD1 signaling for oligodendrocyte survival and remyelination is independently documented by three retrieved MS papers, and SMAD1 is separately placed in Sjögren's by a gland-repair paper, so each disease is known on its own to engage this axis. But no retrieved source states MS and Sjögren's share it, and HOXC8 carries almost no direct disease evidence (no Open Targets signal in either disease, one decades-old structural paper) beyond its target-list overlap with SMAD1's known biology, so the cross-disease claim rests on inference rather than retrieved fact.
support: PMID 39332617 (BMP7 knockdown causes oligodendrocyte apoptosis/demyelination in MS); PMID 35961320 (BMP/SMAD-linked crosstalk disrupts the blood-CNS barrier in neuroinflammatory disease); PMID 35281467 (WGCNA analysis flags BMP-pathway genes as key in MS); PMID 18586880 (SMAD1 implicated in murine lacrimal gland repair after inflammatory injury, Sjögren's-relevant); PMID 15842175 (HOXC8-DNA structural work connecting HOXC8 to osteopontin, an MS-relevant SMAD1/HOXC8 shared target).
how_to_falsify: In oligodendrocyte precursor cultures and in lacrimal/salivary gland organoids, knock down HOXC8 and measure induction of SMAD1's BMP-responsive targets (SPP1, BMP2, SMAD6) after BMP ligand stimulation. If HOXC8 loss does not blunt SMAD1 target induction or repair/differentiation capacity in either tissue, the proposed HOXC8-SMAD1 partnership is not operating there and the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: 6 independent cohort pairs and 182 patient-group comparisons is a reasonable base, but SMAD1 (109/182, 60%) and HOXC8 (98/182, 54%) are mid-pack, not top-ranked, so concordance was violated in roughly 40-46% of comparisons. HOXC8 is the weaker carrying factor — no Open Targets association in either disease and only indirect literature support. The Sjögren's evidence for this module comes from a murine lacrimal-gland-repair study, not human salivary gland or blood, so cross-tissue extrapolation is required. Tissue-generic exclusions (RUNX2, MEF2C, EZH2, FLI1, and others) confirm that generic CNS/immune master regulators were already stripped out, so this account is not simply restating tissue identity; single-view factors (e.g. MEF2C, CTCF, YAP1) were excluded and are not the basis of this story.
